cohort: The study included 188 adult singleton pregnancies with a history of cervical insufficiency (defined as >=1 spontaneous deliveries <28 weeks or failed transvaginal cerclage <34 weeks with cerclage in situ) at a quaternary care center in the United States.
finding: Transabdominal cerclage significantly reduced the risk of preterm delivery <34 weeks compared to transvaginal cerclage in women with a history of recurrent preterm deliveries or failed transvaginal cerclage.
